public_body: Carver Council On Aging Board Of Directors
overall: The AG found the Council on Aging Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on public comment or minutes, and declined to review the filming, adjournment-vote, and website-posting allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the chair barred residents from speaking on non-agenda matters during public comment and abruptly adjourned to cut off further comment.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board was not required to permit public comment during its meetings, and was not required to discuss all matters listed on the meeting notice, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the Board did not create minutes of its September 29 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As the complaint was filed only five days after the meeting in question, minutes were not yet required, and the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the Board refused to let Area 58 television film a meeting, including an August meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We note that the entirety of the September 29 meeting was recorded by Area 58, and any allegation regarding an August meeting was not timely filed.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the Board adjourned its September 29 meeting without a proper motion and vote.
allegations.key_passage: Except in limited ways not applicable here, the Open Meeting Law does not dictate matters of parliamentary procedure such as a requirement that an adjournment be preceded by a motion, second, and vote

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged minutes of prior meetings were not posted online.
allegations.key_passage: nor does the Law require that meeting minutes be posted to a website, see OML 2020-78.
